What's new in SwapMac 0.3.0

  • Developer: a new screen for the space developer tools fill. Build folders in old projects (node_modules, virtual environments, target, Pods), Xcode simulators and runtimes, Docker, local AI models from Ollama, Hugging Face and LM Studio, and package caches. Projects with uncommitted work are never ticked for you, and source files are never touched.
  • Each tool's own clean-up: simulators go through Xcode, Docker prunes itself, package managers clean their own caches. Anything that can't go to the Trash tells you so first, and what downloads again.
  • Any drive: More Scans lists your external drives by name.
  • Shared space: SwapMac tells you when a file shares its space with a copy, so moving it won't free as much.
  • Clearer map: tiles that need a look first or should be kept carry a mark, not just a colour.
  • VoiceOver reads the cleanup review, summary and History more clearly.

What's new in SwapMac 0.2.1

  • Quieter in the background: with its window closed, SwapMac now uses no CPU at all. Live numbers refresh only while you can see them, and more slowly on battery and in Low Power Mode.
  • Activity: a new screen listing cleanups, uninstalls, put-backs, items about to leave the Trash, and updates, each with one thing you can do about it.
  • Settings → Monitoring: turn live numbers off, choose how often they refresh, see what SwapMac itself uses, and choose notifications. They're off unless you turn them on, and never about buying anything.
  • Optional low-space alert when free space drops below 10 GB, at most once a day.

What's new in SwapMac 0.2.0

  • Dashboard: a new first screen with your Mac's storage, memory, battery and what's safe to clear, at a glance.
  • A clearer cleanup: every item says what happens if you clear it, and afterwards a summary shows exactly what moved, what was skipped and why.
  • Cleanup History: grouped by cleanup, with the date each item leaves the Trash. Put Back never overwrites anything, and moving one item offers Undo.
  • A truthful uninstaller: finds an app's helpers, plug-ins and system files too, lets you keep any part, asks for your password once, and says honestly what's left.
  • Calmer setup: SwapMac explains before it asks for access, scans read-only, and shows which folders it couldn't read and why.
  • Where the used space is: what you can review, what macOS manages itself (snapshots, swap, the system) and what couldn't be read.
  • Settings in tabs, a Privacy tab listing exactly what SwapMac sends, clear Pro terms, and SwapMac → Uninstall SwapMac… to remove it completely.

Nothing changes until you choose it, and everything still goes to the Trash first.
